narrative.overview: This portfolio is one person's engineering notebook opened on the table: evidence taped in, margins annotated in plain language. It refuses the category-default developer portfolio and the previous cyber/terminal identity. The world is anchored in real material on hand — MSU-IIT maroon and gold regalia, the olive studio backdrop of the graduation portrait, and the quadrille paper every firmware engineer keeps on the bench. Light theme is the page in daylight; dark theme is the same notebook under a desk lamp. The interface recedes and the evidence leads, so a mixed audience meets a person first, proof second, and a contact route within seconds.
keyCharacteristics: Pages and ruled lists, never grids of identical cards
Photo prints with white borders, slight rotation, and masking tape
One hairline rule weight; depth from offset, softly blurred shadows
Maroon rationed to action and identity; gold only as foil stamping
Handwriting (Caveat) in margins only; tabular mono only for real data

rules.name: One Rule Weight
rules.body: Every separator on the page is the same 1px hairline. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, and placement — never from glow, gradient, or a heavier border.

rules.name: Rationed Maroon
rules.body: Maroon appears where the visitor can act and where the identity lives (binding, buttons, links, active states). Gold foil is stamping only. Neither is decoration.

rules.name: Margin Hand
rules.body: The handwriting face is for five words or fewer in a margin. Body copy, controls, and data stay in their own faces.

rules.name: Evidence First
rules.body: Every claim points at something real: a screenshot, a scan, a repo, a measured figure. Data type is earned by real data.

rules.name: Visible by Default
rules.body: Content is never gated behind an entrance animation. Motion is one authored settle in the hero plus hover micro-motion.

dos: Do present lists as ruled ledger rows with tabular figures
Do present imagery as taped photo prints
Do design both themes as first-class (daylight paper, lamplit night)
Do write labels in plain, grounded language
donts: Don't bring back terminal chrome: HUD brackets, scanlines, neon, carets, ASCII logos, sound effects
Don't use same-size icon cards as page structure
Don't add kickers or numbered eyebrows above headings
Don't use gradient text, glass, glow borders, or hard offset shadows
Don't set body copy in mono or long text in the handwriting face
